newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MILLING WHEAT PRICES ROCKET IN NERVOUS BUDAPEST MKT.
newsitem.headline: MILLING WHEAT PRICES ROCKET IN NERVOUS BUDAPEST MKT.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices rocketed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday as the market's fears of a low quality crop were being confirmed, traders said.
"The only sellers on the market were those who closed earlier buying positions to lock in profits," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
Milling wheat futures rose by between the daily limit of 400 forints per tonne for September and as much as 3,120 forints for one of the freed-up maturities, May.
"The physical and the futures market mutually reinforce each other's rising trend," Szoke said, adding that on the spot market bids have reached 27,000 forints.

The Budapest Commodity Exchange frees up any maturity from limit movements after three consecutive days of limit move in either direction. The limit is set back once the daily price change remains within 400 forints per tonne.

BCE milling wheat futures prices for the 1997 crop were between 28,100 forints for September and 33,710 forints for May while 1998 crop prices were between 26,300 forints for August and 28,950 for October.
Szoke said that although a downward correction could occur for milling wheat, the underlying trend remained a rising one.

Euro wheat futures, despite trading for maturities from August 1998 onward, for which there is no information to trade on, also rose by between 400 and 900 forints to end between 26,000 forints for August and 28,400 for January 1999.

Despite a weak selling side, milling wheat, with 613 lots, accounted for almost half of the BCE's grains futures turnover of 1,334 lots or 766.8 million forints, up from Friday's 425 lots or 188.1 million forints.
Feed wheat and maize futures finished steady to lower in minimal turnover, untraded feed barley was flat.

Sunflower seed rose 200 forints for September to 44,250 and rose by 200 forints for November and December maintaining an inverse spread with November settling at 44,600 and December at 44,400 forints.
